summaries.1: Bab I defines personal data, controllers, processors, data subjects, and the territorial plus extra-territorial scope of Indonesia's PDP Law — including the household-activity exception.
summaries.2: Bab II lists the eight asas (principles) that frame all processing: protection, legal certainty, public interest, benefit, prudence, balance, accountability, and confidentiality.
summaries.3: Bab III distinguishes specific (sensitive) personal data from general personal data.
summaries.4: Bab IV sets data-subject rights: information, access, correction, erasure, withdrawal of consent, objection to automated decisions, restriction, compensation, and portability, plus exceptions.
summaries.5: Bab V describes processing operations, processing principles, CCTV-type visual devices in public places, and joint controllers.
summaries.6: Bab VI is the core operational chapter: legal bases, consent, children's and disability data, DPIA, security, breach notification (3x24 hours), processors, and the DPO.
summaries.7: Bab VII governs domestic and cross-border transfers, including equivalent-protection, adequate binding protection, and consent fallbacks.
summaries.8: Bab VIII provides administrative sanctions, including fines of up to 2% of annual revenue.
summaries.9: Bab IX establishes the presidentially appointed PDP institution, its functions, and its investigative and enforcement powers.
summaries.10: Bab X authorises international cooperation on personal data protection.
summaries.11: Bab XI provides for public participation through education, advocacy, and oversight.
summaries.12: Bab XII covers arbitration, courts, alternative dispute resolution, and electronic evidence.
summaries.13: Bab XIII prohibits unlawful obtaining, disclosing, using, or forging personal data.
summaries.14: Bab XIV sets criminal penalties, including corporate liability and additional sanctions.
summaries.15: Bab XV gave controllers and processors two years from promulgation (until 17 October 2024) to adjust processing.
summaries.16: Bab XVI provides that the Law entered into force on the date of promulgation (17 October 2022).
